messages:
taylor: quick sync — i'm collating notes from the orchestration API consolidation rollout (control-plane -> operator handshake). overall good but noticed two repeat issues: 1) slow scale-up latencies when many cold leases hit at once, 2) ~0.5% of tenant requests failed admission during transient leader elections. opening this thread to list follow-ups and assign owners.

maria: thanks. can you paste a short timeline + symptoms so we can triage?

taylor: timeline (very brief):
- deploy at 09:10 -> consolidated API enabled (canary 10% traffic)
- 09:22 -> canary metrics looked fine
- 09:35 -> traffic ramp to 70%
- 09:40-09:48 -> spikes in scale-up tail latencies (p95 token latency for warmup ops)
- 09:50 -> operator leader flapped after a db failover, ~120 leases retried -> ~0.5% admissions returned "no-capacity"
- 10:05 -> rollback partial config flag for headroom heuristic -> metrics stabilized

raj: two quick observations: first, the consolidated API added extra RPC hop in the admit path (control-plane -> operator -> allocator). that adds coord latency under contention. second, our lease retry backoff is too tight during leader churn so we thundering-herd.

olivia: +1. also saw missing observability tags on the consolidated path (no tenant_id on some operator-side logs) which made root-cause slower. can we add a short-term tag patch?

taylor: propose immediate follow-ups (short):
- patch: add tenant_id and request_id to operator logs (olivia)
- tweak: increase lease-retry jitter/backoff and cap parallel retries per-tenant (raj)
- experiment: add a local admit cache (control-plane) for short-lived warmups to cut RPC roundtrips (sam)
- longer-term: split the admit vs execute surface explicitly in the API — admit should be lightweight sync, execute handled async with traceable tokens (ownership: eng-runtime).

sam: quick note on admit cache idea: simple LRU keyed by model+prefix-hash, TTL 3s, size 2000 entries. cheap and could eliminate ~40% of control-plane->operator hops for bursts. i can prototype a PoC this week.

maria: sounds good. can we also align on SLA for admission failures during leader elections? ops wants an expected failure window and a mitigation plan.

raj: mitigation plan draft:
- leader election: add lease-durable marker so operator can continue admitting while leader is elected (semi-stable fallback)
- admission retry: exponential backoff + per-tenant concurrency cap + random jitter
- graceful degrade: fallback to best-effort cached grants for low-priority tenants (config flag)

infra-bot: deploy-logs: control-plane/2026-03-14T09:08:12Z: migration-applied: orchestration-api-consolidation v2 -> success

taylor: next actions & owners:
- olivia: log tags patch (PR by EOD)
- raj: retry/backoff + concurrency cap rollout (RFC update)
- sam: admit cache PoC + perf measurements (demo Wed)
- taylor: propose API split design doc for admit/execute surface (draft Thu)
- maria: coordinate ops SLA wording and runbook update

maria: assigning owners in jira now. please add ticket IDs here when created. :thumbsup:

taylor: thanks all — also, let's record the API split as a separate RFC so we can involve eng-platform and product early. linking notes to the internal wiki after PRs.

sam: i'll put the PoC branch under /repos/orch/admit-cache and ping here when ready.

olivia: PR opened: #8422 — adds tenant_id/request_id to operator logs. small patch.

raj: created RFC ticket: ORCH-832 (retry & concurrency caps)

maria: jira: PROJ-1290 (SLA & runbook), PROJ-1291 (postmortem notes). closing loop here, moving to async updates.
